findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The constructor's `options` parameter was changed from the zod-inferred `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to the hand-written `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, in which `teamId` is optional even when `scope` is "team". A caller constructing the service with `{ scope: "team", teamId: undefined }` now type-checks (it previously failed to compile against the discriminated-union schema type), and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` passes `undefined` as `teamId` to `TeamRepository.findByIdAndParentId`, which returns no team, so the service silently returns NOTHING_CONDITION and the team owner sees empty insights instead of a compile-time or runtime validation error.

[ADVISORY] The raw org condition interpolates `teamIds` directly into `= ANY(${teamIds})` where `teamIds` can be an empty array when the org has no child teams (and `teamIdsFromOrg.length ? ... : []`). When the org has no child teams, the query sends `= ANY($1)` with an empty-array parameter; depending on Prisma driver serialization this either evaluates to FALSE (matching old `in: []` behavior) or fails with a parameter-type error at runtime — the old Prisma query-builder `in: []` was guaranteed safe, so this path is now unverified against a real Postgres connection for the empty case (no test covers an org with zero teams).

[ADVISORY] The deleted "Caching" describe block removed the only verification that getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions memoize their results, and the rewritten tests never re-verify caching even though the diff changes the cached types from WhereInput to Prisma.Sql. A future refactor that drops or corrupts the cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions memoization (e.g. rebuilding raw SQL with different parameter arrays on every call, or caching a null and then failing on the undefined-check) ships green because no test asserts the second call returns the identical object; users of Insights hit repeated DB round-trips for team/user membership lookups on every insights query.

[ADVISORY] All org- and team-scope conditions are verified only by string-structural toEqual comparisons of Prisma.Sql fragments; the only test that executes conditions against the database (getBaseConditions, line ~477) covers user scope exclusively, so the raw SQL emitted for org/team scopes is never executed. The "isTeamBooking" quoted-identifier, `= ANY(${teamIds})` array parameter binding, and the reduce-built OR chains in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition (insightsBooking.ts lines ~161-179) and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition (~186-203) run in production without ever having been parsed by Postgres in a test; a wrong column name, a casing mismatch against the actual BookingTimeStatusDenormalized schema, or a Prisma array-binding quirk produces a runtime 500 on every org/team insights query that CI never catches.

[ADVISORY] findMany — the service's only data-retrieval method, previously tested end-to-end — is deleted and replaced by getBaseConditions, a public-surface removal with no evidence in the diff that remaining callers were migrated. Any existing caller of InsightsBookingService.findMany (insights API routes, trpc resolvers outside this diff) fails to compile or, in a JS consumer, gets TypeError: service.findMany is not a function at runtime; the diff also silently changes the consumption contract from typed Prisma results to hand-written raw queries the caller must now assemble.

[ADVISORY] getBaseConditions returns NOTHING_CONDITION when both conditions are null, but getAuthorizationConditions is typed as returning Prisma.Sql (never null), so the filterConditions-only and both-null branches are unreachable — and the test suite contains no case for a null filter result flowing through getBaseConditions. The dead branches mask the fact that the real invariant is "auth is never null"; if a future change makes auth nullable (e.g. an options-less service), the combine logic has zero test coverage and the null-handling path that consumers depend on for returning no rows instead of throwing unfiltered queries is unverified.

[ADVISORY] The NOTHING cases are asserted with toEqual(NOTHING_CONDITION) comparing two independently constructed Prisma.Sql objects, which only passes because Prisma.Sql happens to be structurally comparable — there is no test that a NOTHING_CONDITION actually yields zero rows when executed (e.g. via getBaseConditions + $queryRaw). If Prisma.Sql comparison semantics change across @prisma/client versions (private fields, getter-based equality), these tests silently vacuously pass or spuriously fail; more importantly, the security-critical property — non-owner users get zero bookings — is no longer verified by executing the query, only by string comparison.

[BUG] The diff deletes the public findMany() method, the service's only data-retrieval entry point, with no replacement call site added anywhere in the src tree. Any existing consumer of InsightsBookingService.findMany() (insights routes/controllers importing this service) now fails to compile or, if it duck-types, silently loses its query path — the stated intent was 'convert to raw queries', not 'remove the query API'; this is untraceable to the stated requirement.

[BUG] The constructor switches from InsightsBookingServiceOptions (zod-validated schema type) to the new InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions type, which is a hand-maintained parallel of insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema that bypasses validation entirely. Callers can now pass options that violate the discriminated union (e.g. scope 'team' without teamId, or non-numeric userId) with no runtime rejection; the zod schema remains in the file but is only used for type inference, so validation is silently dropped — a public-surface behavior change not required by 'convert to Prisma.sql'.

[ADVISORY] The two 'caching' tests in the integration test file are deleted while the caching implementation (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions) is retained, leaving the memoization behavior completely untested. A regression in the cache (e.g. caching a condition built before membership changes within a request, or the undefined-vs-null sentinel check breaking) ships undetected; the diff rewrote the cached values' type from WhereInput to Prisma.Sql yet removed the only tests exercising repeat-call behavior.

[ADVISORY] InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions duplicates insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema by hand (scope union, userId, orgId, teamId), creating a parallel client+server enumeration with no single source of truth. The next schema change (e.g. adding a scope variant or making teamId required for team scope) updates the zod schema but not the public type (or vice versa), producing drift where TypeScript accepts what zod rejects; whoever edits the schema next gets bitten.

[ADVISORY] getBaseConditions returns NOTHING_CONDITION (1=0) when both auth and filter conditions are null, changing the semantics of 'no filters' from 'match everything the auth allows' to 'match nothing'. A caller invoking getBaseConditions() with no filters set now gets zero rows where the old findMany with no filters would return all authorized rows — the null-fallthrough case is untested and, since no production caller exists in this diff, the first integrator gets a silently empty result set.

[BUG] getAuthorizationConditions()/getFilterConditions() changed their public return type from a Prisma where-input object (Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput) to a raw Prisma.Sql fragment, a sentinel-meaning-change for every existing caller. Any out-of-diff caller that spreads these conditions into a Prisma `where` clause (the original contract) now silently gets a Sql object where an object literal is expected — Prisma ignores it or throws at query-build time, so an authorized user's insights query returns zero rows or errors with no compile-time signal.

[BUG] findMany() was deleted from the public API with no replacement inside the service, forcing all query consumers to hand-write raw SQL against the BookingTimeStatusDenormalized table. Existing callers of service.findMany (the diff shows no migration for them) break at runtime with TypeError: service.findMany is not a function, and every future consumer must duplicate hardcoded column-name strings like "isTeamBooking" that a schema rename will break silently.

[ADVISORY] InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions is a hand-maintained parallel copy of insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema, replacing the validated inferred type at the constructor boundary. The zod schema (the single source of truth for scope/userId/orgId/teamId shape) and the new manual type now drift independently: adding a field or narrowing scope in the schema leaves the constructor type stale, and options are no longer validated at construction since the type substitution abandons the zod parse path.

[ADVISORY] The service now emits PostgreSQL-dialect SQL fragments with "quoted identifiers" and = ANY(array) baked into its return values, coupling a generic service to one database dialect and to literal column names. Any consumer running a non-Postgres Prisma datasource (or a future schema rename of eventTypeId/isTeamBooking) gets SQL errors from strings the TypeScript compiler cannot check; the column names exist only as string literals in eight places across the file.

[ADVISORY] The PR deletes the public findMany() method (the service's only query-executing entry point, taking typed Prisma findManyArgs with select/take/orderBy) and replaces it with getBaseConditions() returning a raw SQL fragment, silently changing the service's contract with no deprecation path. Any existing caller of InsightsBookingService.findMany (routes or other services outside this diff) now fails at compile/runtime with 'findMany is not a function', and even migrated callers lose the ability to pass select/orderBy/pagination — they must hand-write raw SQL against the denormalized table, which the diff provides no helper for.

[ADVISORY] The new hand-maintained InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions type duplicates the existing zod-inferred InsightsBookingServiceOptions / insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema, creating two parallel sources of truth for the same contract. The next schema change (e.g., making teamId required for scope 'team', or adding a field) updates the zod schema but not the hand-written type — or vice versa — and TypeScript will not catch the drift because buildAuthorizationConditions now pattern-matches on options.scope via the manual type while zod parsing elsewhere uses the inferred one; a maintainer editing only one will ship a mismatched contract.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes the entire 'Caching' describe block (previously asserting that repeated getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions calls return the cached object) while the caching logic remains in the service, leaving the caching behavior with zero coverage. A future refactor of getAuthorizationConditions (e.g., dropping the cachedAuthConditions === undefined guard) will pass the full test suite while silently re-running the membership/TeamRepository queries on every call — an N+1 performance regression in the insights endpoints that no test will catch.

[ADVISORY] The final else-branch returning NOTHING_CONDITION in getBaseConditions is unreachable dead code, because getAuthorizationConditions is typed Prisma.Sql (never null) and always returns at least NOTHING_CONDITION, so authConditions is always truthy. The next reader assumes both condition sets can be null and preserves the misleading four-way branch; the reduction opportunities in the filter/else arms can be deleted (the 'else if (filterConditions)' and 'else' arms are dead), and carrying them makes the intent — 'auth conditions are always present' — harder to see.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten assertions compare the exact SQL text of Prisma.Sql objects instead of executing the conditions against the database, so they verify implementation shape rather than query behavior for every authorization path except the single getBaseConditions test. If the generated SQL is semantically broken on a real database (wrong identifier quoting, Prisma array binding to = ANY(...) failing, boolean literal mismatch, missing parentheses changing precedence), the NOTHING/user/org/team tests still pass because they only string-compare; only the user+eventTypeId path in the getBaseConditions test would catch it. The tests also break on any harmless SQL reformatting while passing genuinely broken SQL the author happens to write, inverting the value of the suite. Checked the only test file in the diff, insightsBooking.integration-test.ts — no other test executes these conditions via $queryRaw.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes the two Caching tests ('should cache authorization conditions', 'should cache filter conditions') while the caching logic (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions in insightsBooking.ts) remains fully intact in the source. A regression that breaks memoization (e.g. a future refactor making the cache key stale, or returning a fresh Sql per call that no longer deep-equals) ships silently; the only remaining file is insightsBooking.integration-test.ts and no test there calls getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions twice to assert identity or cache reuse.

[ADVISORY] The new empty-userIds branch in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition (and its twin in buildTeamAuthorizationCondition around line 197-206) — skipping the userId clause and emitting only the teamId = ANY(...) term, or emitting teamId = ANY([]) with an empty array — has no test that triggers it, and the diff also changed the previous behavior where an empty `in: []` array was still emitted as a Prisma condition with different semantics. The org-with-no-verified-users path (all org members unaccepted, so userIdsFromOrg is empty) produces SQL the string-comparison tests never construct; if `= ANY($1)` with an empty array bound as NULL rather than an empty Postgres array (a known Prisma driver edge case depending on how the array is passed), org owners of empty orgs get zero rows or errors in production with green tests. Checked insightsBooking.integration-test.ts — every org/team test seeds memberships with at least one accepted user.

[ADVISORY] The single behavioral test executes getBaseConditions only for the user-scope + eventTypeId path, so the combining logic's auth-only, filter-only, and both-null branches in getBaseConditions (insightsBooking.ts lines 68-79) are never executed against the database by any test in this diff. The branch that returns NOTHING_CONDITION when both conditions are null and the single-condition passthrough branches (e.g. filterConditions null when no filters passed) are dead-to-tests; if concatenating two Prisma.Sql fragments via Prisma.sql`(${a}) AND (${b})` produced invalid parameter ordering or a type mismatch for the filter-only case, no test would fail — every other test string-compares instead of executing.

[ADVISORY] The public method findMany(findManyArgs) is deleted and replaced by getBaseConditions(), which silently breaks every existing caller of the service. Any caller (in-tree pages/APIs or downstream packages) that constructs InsightsBookingService and calls findMany gets a runtime 'is not a function' TypeError after deploy — a rolling deploy where this lib ships before all call sites are migrated will serve 500s on the insights pages instead of booking data.

[ADVISORY] The constructor's options type is widened from the zod-validated InsightsBookingServiceOptions to a hand-written InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions that makes teamId optional for all scopes, so a 'team'-scope call without teamId is no longer caught at the type level. A call site passing scope:'team' without teamId compiles cleanly, then buildTeamAuthorizationCondition interpolates undefined into Prisma.sql`"teamId" = ${options.teamId}`, which throws a Prisma parameter error (or matches nothing) at query time instead of being rejected up front — the insights query path 500s for that team's users.

[ADVISORY] In buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, an empty teamIds array is passed unconditionally as `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))`, and unlike the userId branch it is not guarded on length, so an org with no child teams still embeds the empty-array parameter. For a freshly created org with zero teams, the generated SQL relies on ANY(empty) evaluating false; if any future driver/dialect or query-rewrite path serializes the empty array parameter as NULL, `teamId = ANY(NULL)` yields NULL and the condition silently fails closed — behavior differs from the userId branch which is explicitly guarded, leaving an inconsistent invariant the next editor will trip over.

[BUG] The constructor now takes InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions directly instead of parsing through insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema, so unvalidated/undefined values (e.g. userId: undefined or a garbage scope) flow straight into the SQL builders. A caller passing a partially-populated options object (previously rejected by the zod discriminated union with a clear validation error) now builds Prisma.sql`"userId" = ${undefined}` — the parameter binds as null, every comparison is false, and the API returns an empty result set with HTTP 200: an unauthorized-shaped silent failure reported as success, with no error and no log.

[ADVISORY] The public findMany method was deleted and replaced by getBaseConditions, which only returns the WHERE-clause Sql — the class no longer executes queries itself. Any in-repo or downstream caller of InsightsBookingService.findMany (this is an exported service in packages/lib) now fails at runtime with 'service.findMany is not a function', producing a 500 on whatever insights route still invokes it; callers must also hand-compose the raw query exactly as the test does, and a caller that forgets to interpolate baseConditions into a WHERE clause silently loses all authorization filtering.

goldens.comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The constructor's `options` parameter was changed from the zod-inferred `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to the hand-written `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, in which `teamId` is optional even when `scope` is "team". adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` and changes the constructor to accept it (`options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`), where `teamId?: number` is optional regardless of `scope`. This makes `{ scope: "team", teamId: undefined }` type-check at call sites. At runtime, `buildAuthorizationConditions()` routes `scope === "team"` to `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition(this.options)`, and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` passes `options.teamId` directly into `TeamRepository.findByIdAndParentId({ id: options.teamId, parentId: options.orgId, ... })`. If `teamId` is `undefined`, `childTeamOfOrg` will be falsy and the method returns `NOTHING_CONDITION`, yielding empty insights instead of a validation error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The raw org condition interpolates `teamIds` directly into `= ANY(${teamIds})` where `teamIds` can be an empty array when the org has no child teams (and `teamIdsFromOrg.length ? ... : []`). adjudication.rationale: In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, the first branch always emits `Prisma.sql`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)`` where `teamIds` comes from `teamsFromOrg`/`childTeamIds` and can be `[]` if the org has no child teams. The diff does not guard this empty-array case (unlike the prior Prisma `in: []` which is known-safe), and there is no added test covering an org with zero teams to validate how Prisma serializes an empty array for `ANY($1)` against Postgres. Whether it errors or simply evaluates false depends on driver/typing, so it’s a specific unverified edge case introduced by the change rather than a clearly provable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The deleted "Caching" describe block removed the only verification that getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions memoize their results, and the rewritten tests never re-verify caching even though the diff changes the cached types from WhereInput to Prisma.Sql. adjudication.rationale: The diff deletes the entire `describe("Caching")` block that previously asserted a second call to `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` returns the same value, and no new test reintroduces that behavior. Meanwhile the implementation changes cached types from `BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` to `Prisma.Sql` (`cachedAuthConditions?: Prisma.Sql; cachedFilterConditions?: Prisma.Sql | null;`), so caching semantics are still relevant and now unverified. The current code still memoizes via `=== undefined` checks, so this is not a present functional bug, but it is a concrete test-coverage regression tied to the change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the service from Prisma `WhereInput` objects to raw `Prisma.Sql` fragments (e.g., `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` now build SQL with quoted identifiers, `= ANY(${...})` array binding, and `reduce`-built OR chains). The only newly added test that actually runs the condition via `prisma.$queryRaw` is `getBaseConditions` and it uses `scope: "user"` (so it doesn’t exercise org/team SQL). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap for newly introduced raw SQL logic, but not a proven runtime defect from the diff alone.
